codeReview.summary: The refactor cleanly delegates interpreter lifecycle to InterpreterPool via a new _ManagedAgentContext async context manager. The implementation correctly acquires an interpreter from the pool, passes it to the agent builder, releases it on normal exit, nulls agent.interpreter to prevent double-shutdown, and releases on builder failure before re-raising. The only production caller (websocket endpoint) already uses `async with`, and tests were updated to match the new wrapper contract. No blocking issues were found.

issues.description: _ManagedAgentContext.__aexit__ nulls self._agent.interpreter but does not null self._interpreter. If the context manager were somehow re-entered (not the intended one-shot usage), release() would be called again. Since InterpreterPool.release swallows all exceptions, this is harmless in practice, but nulling self._interpreter would make the guard more robust.

The new tests cover release on normal exit and release on builder failure, but there is no explicit test for release when an exception is raised inside the `async with` block. Since __aexit__ returns False and runs the same cleanup regardless of exc_type, this is implicitly correct, but an explicit test would harden the contract.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The runtime-cleanup-worker skill example handoff references a test named `test_build_chat_agent_context_uses_backend_owned_builder`, but the actual test in the codebase is `test_build_chat_agent_context_uses_canonical_builder`. The skill example is out of sync with the live test name.

The interpreter lifecycle delegation pattern (acquire via InterpreterPool, wrap in _ManagedAgentContext, null agent.interpreter on exit, release via pool) is a new canonical pattern that should be documented in runtime-patterns.md so future workers don't reintroduce inline shutdown in AgentRuntime or transport layers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/runtime-patterns.md documents the old state where 'AgentRuntime.__init__ accepts and stores interpreter but does not currently use it in chat_turn()'. This is now superseded by the pool-managed lifecycle in chat_runtime.py.

summary: The feature passes review. The implementation is architecturally sound, handles edge cases (builder failure, None interpreter), and aligns with the existing InterpreterPool contract. Two non-blocking observations were noted: a minor defensiveness gap in _ManagedAgentContext and a missing explicit test for exception-during-block cleanup. Shared state observations note skill example drift and a documentation gap in runtime-patterns.md.
